territorial_scope.description: Applies to U.S. IaaS providers and U.S. IaaS products (those owned by U.S. persons or operated in the U.S.), reaches foreign customers and foreign resellers, and allows special measures naming foreign jurisdictions or foreign persons.

evidence.quote: United States Infrastructure as a Service product or U.S. IaaS product means any Infrastructure as a Service product owned by any United States person or operated within the territory of the United States.

summary.short: Subpart D rule (§§ 7.300–7.310) requiring U.S. infrastructure-as-a-service providers to run customer identification programs for foreign accounts, certify them to the Department, report foreign training of large AI models with potential malicious cyber-enabled capabilities, and accept special measures and penalties.
summary.long: Subpart D (§§ 7.300–7.310) of a Department of Commerce rule implementing Executive Orders 13984 and 14110 requires U.S. infrastructure-as-a-service (IaaS) providers to run a written Customer Identification Program (CIP) that verifies the identity of foreign customers and beneficial owners, and to ensure foreign resellers maintain equivalent CIPs (§§ 7.302–7.303). Providers must submit CIP certification forms and annual certifications, notify material changes, and keep records for at least two years (§ 7.304). The Department may conduct compliance assessments (§ 7.305). The Secretary may exempt providers with a finding under an Abuse of IaaS Products Deterrence Program (§ 7.306), and may impose special measures, such as prohibitions or conditions on accounts, on foreign jurisdictions or persons found to use IaaS products for malicious cyber-enabled activity (§ 7.307). Providers must report covered transactions that could train a large AI model with potential malicious cyber-enabled capabilities within 15 calendar days (§ 7.308). Violations carry civil penalties under IEEPA (the greater of $250,000 per violation or twice the transaction amount) and criminal fines up to $1,000,000 or imprisonment up to 20 years for willful violations (§ 7.309).

notes: Text supplied is Subpart D (§§ 7.300-7.310) only; the preamble, other subparts, the Federal Register citation and date are not in the document. Registry status (pending) is not verifiable from the text. No named firms appear; providers and resellers are addressed generically. Internal issues: § 7.308(c)(4) gives 15 calendar dates (likely days); Federal Register citations are blank ('published in the Federal Register .') in § 7.301, § 7.307(a)(5) and § 7.308(b)(2); 'Department' and 'Secretary' are used for overlapping functions (§ 7.305 vs § 7.306); 'technical parameters of concern' in the large AI model definition is undefined and § 7.308(b)(2) defers the technical conditions to interpretive rules the text says will be published. § 7.307(a)(6) gives only a 180-day effective date for special measures. No private right of action is stated (left null in enforcement, not coded here). Cross-references to 15 CFR chapter VII and subpart B are disclaimed or internal and not coded as relations.
